unit: Unit 13: Making Your Computer Easier to Use
title: Settings that adapt to you
drDigitalIntro:
Your computer can change to suit your eyes, your hands and your attention.
• These are called accessibility settings, and they are for everyone — not only for people with a diagnosis.
• If you squint at small text, hunt for the mouse pointer, or find moving windows distracting, there is a setting for it.
• Nothing here is permanent. Every switch in this unit turns back off the same way it turned on.
• Over the next few lessons you will try each one on a practice computer, so you can decide what you actually want.
drDigitalSuccess: Now let's go and try them.
drDigitalHint: Read along and click Continue when you are ready.
